tasks.title: The rate for SERVO_TILT to suit your servo
tasks.statement: A gimbal servo turns by **{theta}°** when the pulse changes by 1000 µs (1000 → 2000). What `rate` in the `servo` command is needed for SERVO_TILT in CAMSTAB mode to compensate the frame tilt exactly (gimbal_mode NORMAL)?
tasks.solution: servoTable(): the pulse grows by rate·angle_in_decidegrees/50 = rate/5 µs per degree. The servo gives 1000/θ µs per degree, so rate = 5·1000/θ (in the CLI — an integer, the nearest one; up to 100 is allowed, so θ ≥ 50°).

tasks.title: The pitch servo pulse in CAMSTAB
tasks.statement: SERVO_TILT, CAMSTAB is on, `servo 0 1000 2000 {mid} {rate} -1`. The frame is tilted in pitch by **{p}°** (attitude in the firmware is in tenths of a degree). What pulse (µs) will the pitch servo get in Betaflight 2025.12 (the formula is the same as in 4.5)?
tasks.solution: Pulse = constrain(middle + rate·(p·10)/50, min, max). The division is integer, and C truncates toward zero (−19.6 → −19). Then clipping to 1000…2000: at rate 100 and |p| ≥ 25° the servo hits the stop.

tasks.title: An elevon from smix rules
tasks.statement: CUSTOMAIRPLANE, the elevon rules: `smix 0 3 4 {kr} 0 0 100 0` (RC roll) and `smix 1 3 5 {kp} 0 0 100 0` (RC pitch); `servo 3 1000 2000 1500 100 -1`. The roll stick is at **{r} µs**, pitch at **{q} µs** (`mid_rc` 1500). What is the pulse on servo 3?
tasks.solution: servoMixer(): every rule = (rc − 1500)·rate/100 (integer, truncated toward zero); the ±500 clipping (a travel width of 1000, min 0 %, max 100 %) does not act here, because |rc − 1500| ≤ 300. The sum × the servo rate 100/100 + middle 1500, then clipping to 1000…2000.

tasks.title: How long the travel takes with smix speed
tasks.statement: An `smix` rule with speed **{s}**, a PID loop rate of **{f} kHz**. The rule input changes in a step by **{d}** units (1 unit ≈ 1 µs). After how many milliseconds will the rule output catch up with the input?
tasks.solution: servoMixer() is called every PID loop (subTaskMotorUpdate) and moves the output by no more than speed per loop: ⌈d/s⌉ loops of 1/f ms.
